title: Hydraulic Press Pascal Dynamics — Force Multiplication & Fluid Power
topic: Fluid Mechanics & Mechanical Engineering — Pascal's Principle in Hydraulic Systems
pedagogical_goal: Master Pascal's Law (P₁=P₂) by interactively exploring how a small input force on a small piston generates a massive output force on a large piston through an incompressible fluid, while conserving energy via displacement trade-off (F₁d₁=F₂d₂). Visualize real-time pressure fields, fluid particle kinetics, and the nonlinear force-displacement relationship governing industrial press brakes, car brakes, and aerospace actuators.

fundamental_laws: Pascal's Principle: ΔP = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ — pressure applied to confined fluid transmits undiminished
Force Multiplication: F₂ = F₁ × (A₂/A₁) = F₁ × (d₂²/d₁²) — output force scales with area ratio
Volume Conservation (Incompressible Flow): A₁·v₁ = A₂·v₂ = Q — volumetric flow rate constant
Displacement Trade-off: x₂ = x₁ × (A₁/A₂) — large force moves small distance
Work Conservation (Ideal): W_in = F₁·x₁ = F₂·x₂ = W_out — energy conserved, power P = F·v
Hydraulic Power: P_hyd = ΔP × Q = (F₁/A₁) × (A₁·v₁) = F₁·v₁ = F₂·v₂
Dynamic Pressure (Bernoulli + Losses): P_dynamic = ½ρv² + μ·(dv/dy) — minor for quasi-static press

components.description: Layer 1: Industrial test cell with 50mm isometric grid, floor mounting bolts, overhead crane rail, and graduated pressure scale rulers on left/right margins

Layer 2: Massive C-frame hydraulic press (H-frame variant) occupying 72% viewport — 420×380mm central silhouette with 45mm thick columns, 60mm crown, 50mm bed, 4×M24 anchor bolts, T-slotted work table, and removable die set. Closed Bezier path: M60,80 C60,40 120,20 180,20 L780,20 C840,20 900,40 900,80 L900,400 C900,440 840,460 780,460 L180,460 C120,460 60,440 60,400 Z with internal cutouts for cylinders

Layer 3: Dual hydraulic cylinders with dynamic fluid columns — input cylinder (Ød1) at left pump station, output cylinder (Ød2) at press ram. Each cylinder filled with radialGradient (id=fluidGrad1, fluidGrad2) transitioning from fluid_base (0% pressure) to fluid_high (100% pressure) with animated Gaussian turbulence filter (feTurbulence baseFrequency=0.02 numOctaves=3) and feDisplacementMap scale=3 driven by P_Pa. Connecting manifold shows pressure wave propagation via animated dasharray offset

Layer 4: 32 animated entities — (1) Input piston rod translating vertically with scaleY pulse on stroke, (2) Output ram translating with scaleY inverse ratio, (3) 20 fluid particles (circles r=2-4) flowing in manifold with velocity v1/v2, color-shifted by local pressure, (4) 4 pump gear teeth rotating at ω=Q/(π·r³), (5) 4 pressure wave rings expanding from pump outlet, (6) Workpiece (metal blank) compressing under ram with plastic deformation scaleX tween

Layer 5: Live HUD — (a) Digital pressure gauge (Ø60mm) at pump with needle tweening 0-400 bar, (b) Force badges: F₁=XXX N at input piston, F₂=XXX kN at ram, (c) Equation banner: 'P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ = XXX bar' anchored to manifold, (d) Displacement rulers: x₁=XXX mm, x₂=XXX mm with vernier, (e) Power meter: P_hyd=XXX kW, (f) Efficiency tag: η=XX%, (g) Stroke limit indicator: red zone at stroke_mm

lifecycle_rules: Use React useRef for all SVG node references (cylinders, pistons, particles, gauges, text)
Wrap all animations in gsap.context(() => { ... }, scopeRef) inside useEffect with [] deps for auto-cleanup

Animate REAL kinetic transforms: piston rods use y translation (gsap.to(pistonRef, { y: -x1_mm, duration: 0.1, ease: 'none' })), ram uses y translation with inverse ratio, pump gears use rotation (rotation: 360 * sim_time_s * Q_m3_s), fluid particles use x/y translation with velocity-proportional speed
STRICT PROHIBITION on strokeDasharray-only 'fake flow' — particles must translate in physical space
Smooth parameter transitions: gsap.to(derivedState, { duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.out', onUpdate: forceUpdate }) for F1, d1, d2, Q changes
Pressure wave rings: gsap.fromTo(ringRef, { scale: 0, opacity: 0.6 }, { scale: 2, opacity: 0, duration: 0.8, repeat: -1, stagger: 0.2 })
Workpiece deformation: gsap.to(workpieceRef, { scaleX: 1 - x2_mm/stroke_mm*0.15, transformOrigin: 'center', duration: 0.1 })

pedagogical_callouts.title: Pascal's Principle Activated
pedagogical_callouts.text: Pressure applied to the small input piston (F₁/A₁) transmits undiminished through the incompressible hydraulic fluid to the large output piston. Observe the pressure gauge — it reads identically at both cylinders regardless of diameter.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Force Multiplication in Action
pedagogical_callouts.text: The output force F₂ = F₁ × (A₂/A₁) = F₁ × (d₂/d₁)². With d₁=25mm and d₂=200mm, area ratio = 64×. Your 500 N input becomes 32 kN output (minus losses). Watch the force badges update live as you adjust diameters.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Energy Conservation — The Displacement Trade-off
pedagogical_callouts.text: Volume conservation demands A₁·x₁ = A₂·x₂. The ram moves only 1/64th the distance of the input piston. Work in = Work out (ideal): F₁·x₁ = F₂·x₂. Power P = F₁·v₁ = F₂·v₂ remains constant. Adjust flow rate Q to see velocity scaling.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Real-World Losses & Dynamic Effects
pedagogical_callouts.text: Efficiency η < 1.0 captures seal friction, fluid compressibility, and leakage. Viscosity μ creates pressure drop ΔP = 32μLv/d² in lines. Reynolds number indicates flow regime — keep Re < 2300 for laminar. At high cycle rates, fluid inertia and water hammer appear.

technical_requirements.styling: Tailwind CSS utility classes with dark glassmorphism (bg-slate-950/80 backdrop-blur-sm border-slate-700) and CSS variables for theme colors
technical_requirements.no_broken_dependencies: All icons are inline SVG (gauge needles, pump gears, pressure waves, force arrows). No external image assets. GSAP loaded via CDN in index.html. Zero runtime dependencies beyond React/GSAP.
